editorial:
Imagine you are dropped right into the middle of Rome during the time of Mussolini. A scary killer is on the loose, targeting young girls, and the whole city is on edge. You get to see how the police and the government handle the panic, but it is not a standard police show. Instead, you see how the leaders use the fear of the public to make themselves look strong. The vibe is a weird mix of a dark crime story and a biting comedy that mocks how powerful people manipulate the truth to stay in charge.

What really works here is how the movie shows the press twisting the news to fit a specific story. The acting is solid, and the way it builds tension without being too slow is great. While some parts might feel a bit old-school, the message about fake news still feels very current. You should definitely check this out if you like stories about politics and crime. For the best experience, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection to catch all the great detail in the old city streets.
endingExplained: The movie ends by showing that the truth does not actually matter to the people in power. Even though the killer is found, the government cares more about their image than justice. They twist the final facts to make the fascist regime look like the heroes. You realize the real monster is not just the killer, but the system that lies to everyone to keep control of the city.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves political thrillers and old Italian cinema.
